input.requirements_spec: Enable post-publish performance tracking, automated payment calculation (base_fee + performance bonus), weekly batch settlement via the existing Payment Service, and analytics dashboards for both brands (campaign ROI) and creators (earnings detail). Key requirements: 7-day tracking window, Celery periodic metric sync, bonus calculated from campaign-defined threshold rules, idempotent settlement, all monetary math in Decimal. See full spec C1-05 for 7 user stories, 10 edge cases, and 5 NFRs.
input.system_context: Existing FastAPI microservice (xhs-campaign-service) with layered architecture: Model → Repository → Service → API. Existing entities: User (with roles creator/brand/admin), Campaign, Application (with negotiated base_fee as Numeric), ContentSubmission, ContentVersion, Review. External services: Payment Service (transfer API with idempotency_key support), Content Service (provides note metrics: views, likes, comments, shares, clicks), Notification Service. Infrastructure: PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery with beat scheduler. Auth via X-User-Id header + role checks through require_role dependency.
input.constraints: All monetary values use Numeric(10,2) in DB and Python Decimal in code — float is prohibited. Settlement must be idempotent (crash-safe restartable batches). Analytics queries must respond within 500ms p95 for campaigns with up to 500 creators. Batch settlement runs weekly (Monday 02:00 UTC).

new_files.responsibility: PerformanceMetric SQLAlchemy model — stores periodic metric snapshots for tracked content
Settlement and PaymentRecord SQLAlchemy models — financial records for calculated and settled payments
Pydantic schemas: PublishConfirmation, SettlementResponse, PaymentRecordResponse, EarningsSummaryResponse, SettlementBatchRequest/Response
SettlementRepository — CRUD and query methods for Settlement, PaymentRecord, PerformanceMetric
SettlementService — publish confirmation handling, payment calculation, batch settlement orchestration
AnalyticsService — campaign-level and creator-level analytics aggregation
BonusCalculator — pure function: given metrics + bonus rules, returns bonus breakdown using Decimal arithmetic
Settlement API router — publish confirmation, earnings view, settlement detail, admin batch trigger
Analytics API router — campaign analytics for brands, performance metrics for creators
Celery tasks — sync_performance_metrics (every 4h), close_tracking_windows (daily), calculate_payments (daily), run_settlement_batch (weekly Monday 02:00 UTC)

module_design.dependency_graph: API routers → Services → Repositories → Models. BonusCalculator is a pure utility used by SettlementService. Celery tasks call SettlementService methods. AnalyticsService reads from SettlementRepository + PerformanceMetric data. No circular dependencies.

integration_points.purpose: Fetch performance metrics (views, likes, comments, shares, clicks) for published notes
integration_points.error_handling: Retry with exponential backoff (4h → 8h → 16h). Log warning if no successful sync for 48h. If zero snapshots exist at window close, flag for admin review.
integration_points.notes: post_id extracted from post_url. Content Service is the source of truth for metrics.

integration_points.purpose: Execute monetary transfers to creator wallets
integration_points.interface: HTTP POST /api/internal/transfers with {creator_id, amount, currency: 'CNY', idempotency_key}
integration_points.error_handling: Per-record error handling. On transfer failure: mark PaymentRecord as failed with error_message, continue with next record. On platform_balance_insufficient: halt batch, alert admin.
integration_points.notes: Payment Service guarantees idempotency via idempotency_key. Safe to retry.

integration_points.purpose: Read campaign bonus rules and trigger campaign completion
integration_points.interface: Internal method calls within the same codebase (Campaign model has bonus_rules JSON field)
integration_points.called_by: BonusCalculator reads campaign.bonus_rules. SettlementService triggers campaign status → 'completed' when all settlements for a campaign are settled.
integration_points.error_handling: Transactional — campaign status update is in the same DB transaction as settlement status update.

integration_points.purpose: Notify creators of payment calculation and settlement events
integration_points.called_by: SettlementService after payment calculation (notify creator of amount) and after settlement (notify creator of payout)
integration_points.error_handling: Fire-and-forget with async retry. Notification failure must not block settlement.

technical_decisions.decision: Use Python Decimal with Numeric(10,2) for all monetary values
technical_decisions.justification: Float arithmetic produces rounding errors (e.g., 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004) that are unacceptable for financial calculations. Even 0.01 CNY discrepancy at scale causes reconciliation nightmares.
alternatives_considered: Integer cents (store 10000 for 100.00 CNY): more performant but harder to read in DB queries and API responses, higher risk of conversion bugs at boundaries.
Float with rounding at output: fragile — rounding must be applied at every intermediate step, easy to miss one and accumulate errors.
technical_decisions.implementation: DB columns: Numeric(10, 2). Python: from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_HALF_UP. Pydantic schemas: condecimal(max_digits=10, decimal_places=2). JSON serialization: string representation to avoid JavaScript float coercion.

technical_decisions.decision: Idempotent settlement using composite idempotency_key with unique constraint
technical_decisions.justification: Celery tasks can be retried on failure. Settlement batch jobs can crash mid-processing and restart. Without idempotency, creators could receive duplicate payments — a critical financial risk.
alternatives_considered: Database transaction with SELECT FOR UPDATE: prevents duplicates but doesn't help with cross-service idempotency (Payment Service needs its own idempotency_key).
Distributed lock (Redis): adds infrastructure dependency and doesn't survive Redis restart.
technical_decisions.implementation: Settlement.idempotency_key = f'{application_id}:{campaign_id}:{window_end.isoformat()}' with UNIQUE constraint. PaymentRecord.idempotency_key = f'pay:{settlement_id}' passed to Payment Service transfer API. If IntegrityError on insert, skip (already processed).

technical_decisions.decision: Configurable bonus rules stored as JSON on Campaign model, evaluated by a pure BonusCalculator utility
technical_decisions.justification: Different campaigns have different bonus structures. Storing rules as structured JSON on the campaign allows brands to define custom thresholds without schema changes. A pure calculator function (no side effects, no DB access) is trivially testable.
alternatives_considered: Separate BonusRule table with FK to Campaign: more normalized but adds query complexity and JOIN overhead for a field that's always read with the campaign.
Hardcoded formula: inflexible, requires code changes for each new bonus structure.
technical_decisions.implementation: Campaign.bonus_rules: JSON field containing [{metric: str, threshold: int, bonus_amount: str (Decimal-serialized)}]. BonusCalculator.calculate(metrics: PerformanceMetric, rules: list[BonusRule]) -> BonusBreakdown. Returns list of triggered bonuses with individual amounts, capped at (max_fee - base_fee).

technical_decisions.decision: Batch settlement via Celery periodic task processing in chunks of 100
technical_decisions.justification: Processing all calculated payments in one go risks timeout and memory issues. Chunking with per-record error handling ensures one failure doesn't block the entire batch. Celery beat provides reliable scheduling with visibility into task state.
alternatives_considered: Real-time settlement (pay immediately on calculation): higher infrastructure load, harder to audit, harder to implement batch-level error handling.
Database-driven job queue (pg_cron): fewer moving parts but less visibility and harder to monitor than Celery.
technical_decisions.implementation: Celery beat schedule: run_settlement_batch every Monday 02:00 UTC. Task queries Settlement WHERE status='calculated' AND calculated_at < cutoff, ordered by calculated_at ASC. Processes in chunks of 100. Each chunk is a separate DB transaction. Failed records remain in 'settlement_failed' and are retried in the next batch.

publish_to_payment_flow.description: End-to-end flow from content publication to creator payout

steps.system_behavior: Validate submission is in 'approved' status. Create PerformanceMetric record with is_final=false. Set submission status to 'published'. Calculate tracking_window_end = now + 7 days. Return tracking info.

steps.action: Celery task sync_performance_metrics runs every 4 hours
steps.system_behavior: Query all PerformanceMetric records where is_final=false AND tracking_window_end > now. For each, call Content Service to fetch current metrics. Create new PerformanceMetric snapshot row.
steps.data_written: New PerformanceMetric row per tracked submission

steps.system_behavior: Query PerformanceMetric records where is_final=false AND tracking_window_end <= now. For each, mark the latest snapshot as is_final=true. These are now ready for payment calculation.

steps.action: Celery task calculate_payments runs daily (after close_tracking_windows)
steps.system_behavior: Query final PerformanceMetric records that have no corresponding Settlement. For each: (a) Load the application to get base_fee, (b) Load campaign to get bonus_rules, (c) Call BonusCalculator.calculate(metrics, rules), (d) Create Settlement record with idempotency_key. All monetary math uses Decimal.

steps.action: Celery task run_settlement_batch runs Monday 02:00 UTC
steps.system_behavior: Create SettlementBatch record. Query Settlements WHERE status='calculated'. Process in chunks of 100. For each: (a) Set status → pending_settlement, (b) Create PaymentRecord, (c) Call Payment Service transfer API with idempotency_key, (d) On success: PaymentRecord.status → succeeded, Settlement.status → settled. On failure: PaymentRecord.status → failed, Settlement.status → settlement_failed with error_message. Update SettlementBatch counters.
Query Settlements for creator_id. Aggregate totals. Return paginated list with bonus_breakdown detail.

Verify brand owns the campaign. Query final PerformanceMetric records for all submissions in this campaign. Aggregate: sum(views) → total_reach, sum(likes+comments+shares) → total_engagement, sum(clicks) → total_clicks. Query Settlements for total_spend. Compute cost_per_engagement and roi_ratio using Decimal.
steps.optimization: For v1, compute on-the-fly with indexed queries. Cache results in Redis for 5 minutes. For scale: migrate to materialized view refreshed hourly.
